hints.title: Monotonic Eating Speed
hints.text: If Koko eats at speed k, the total hours required decreases monotonically as k increases. What is the smallest and largest possible eating speed?

hints.title: Feasibility Threshold Property
hints.text: If speed k is sufficient to finish within h hours, any speed greater than k is also sufficient. The goal is to find the boundary of feasibility.

hints.title: Answer Space Range Halving
hints.text: Set search range left = 1 and right = max(piles). While left < right, pick mid and sum ceil(pile / mid) across all piles. If total hours <= h, the speed is feasible, so set right = mid. Otherwise set left = mid + 1. Return left upon convergence.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of banana piles (1 <= N <= 10^4)
max(P): maximum bananas in a single pile (1 <= max(P) <= 10^9)
complexity.notes: Binary search over speeds [1, max(piles)] with O(N) feasibility check per step.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing each speed k linearly starting from 1 takes O(N * max(P)) time. With max(P) = 10^9 and N = 10^4, this requires 10^13 operations, which results in TLE.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Searching the answer space reduces the number of feasibility checks from max(P) to log2(max(P)) ≈ 30 evaluations, with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing the monotonic predicate f(k) <= h, avoiding floating-point precision issues using integer arithmetic (p + k - 1) // k, and maintaining the correct invariant right = mid.
